name: Koeberliniaceae

lineage_context.teaching_goal: Teach Koeberlinia spinosa as a nearly leafless photosynthetic thorn-shrub with green branches, tiny ephemeral leaves, 4-merous bisexual flowers with 8 stamens and a berry—an extreme Brassicales body plan.

project_scope.note: Accepted current species; native from California to Texas and Mexico, with three accepted varieties.

family_diagnostics.where_to_look_first: Start with the green thorny branches. True leaves are minute and quickly shed, so most photosynthesis occurs in the green stems.
family_diagnostics.vegetative: Dense shrub or small tree with long green thorn-tipped branches; leaves tiny, scale-like/short-lived.
family_diagnostics.reproductive: Bisexual 4-merous flowers: 4 sepals, 4 petals and 8 stamens around a single ovary.
family_diagnostics.fruit: Small berry, contrasting with the siliques/silicles of Brassicaceae.
family_diagnostics.field_tip: Almost leafless green thorn-shrub + 4-part bisexual flower + 8 stamens + berry = Koeberliniaceae/Koeberlinia.

visual_lesson.teaching_order: green thorn branch → tiny leaf → 4-part flower → eight stamens → berry → Brassicaceae comparison → variety caution
visual_lesson.intro: Crown of thorns is a great reminder that belonging to Brassicales does not mean looking like a mustard. It has turned green branches into the main photosynthetic surface.

steps.title: 1 · Treat the green branch as the leaf substitute
steps.look_for: Long green branches ending in thorns, with almost no persistent foliage.

steps.title: 2 · Find the tiny short-lived leaves
steps.look_for: Minute leaves before they are shed.
steps.why_it_matters: Explains why the mature plant looks leafless.

steps.title: 3 · Count 4 + 4 + 8
steps.look_for: Four sepals, four petals and eight stamens.
steps.why_it_matters: A clean reproductive formula for the family.

steps.title: 4 · Find the berry
steps.look_for: Small fleshy berry with persistent style tip.
steps.why_it_matters: Separates this Brassicales family from mustard siliques/silicles.

steps.title: 5 · Keep varieties out of the family lesson
steps.look_for: K. spinosa has accepted varieties including spinosa, tenuispina and wivaggii.
steps.why_it_matters: The project source is species-level; thorn proportions/flower measurements belong in later variety work.

comparisons.title: Koeberliniaceae vs Brassicaceae
comparisons.rule: Both are Brassicales, but Koeberlinia is a woody nearly leafless thorn shrub with 8 stamens and a berry; Brassicaceae is mostly herbaceous with 6 tetradynamous stamens and a silique/silicle.

visual_lesson.caveat: Do not force a variety from thorn length alone in the family lesson. FNA recognizes three varieties with overlapping quantitative characters.

genera.fast_cue: green thorn branches + tiny deciduous leaves + 4-part flower with 8 stamens + berry

taxonomy_reconciliation.note: Accepted; native range includes Texas; current Kew recognizes three varieties.

visual_targets.annotation_goal: label photosynthetic stem, thorn tip and ephemeral leaf
defer thorn-length variety key to species lane
